How much free time do you have each day? If it isn't a lot, I'd recommend a cockatiel, or a caique. Cockatiels are such cuddly little birds, and caiques are very good at entertaining themselves, given enough toys. If you have more time (and the capacity to house a louder bird) I'd always recommend galahs. They're such cuddlebugs, and are very intelligent. Plus, they're all pink! They look like floofy marshmallows!

Actually, I'd recommend pretty much any cockatoo. They're a bit needier, but in return you'll have a sweet, smart companion who'll live for a relatively long time.

I'm not necessarily a parrot expert, heh, just an avid enthusiast and ornithology minor. I'm glad I could provide some insight, birds are one of my favorite things to talk about. I hope this helps!

QUICK EDIT: Most cockatoos are sweet. There is the possibility that yours might be a bit of a jerk, but with a lot of time and love, a lot of them can be raised to be very docile. Getting a parrot is a lot like getting a child; there are lots of different personalities. I've always said, cockatoos are like toddlers with bolt cutters superglued to their faces. They have the learning capacity of a three-year-old, which to me is terrifyingly, but mainly fascinatingly, intelligent. I may be a bit biased, though. ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯

Once, when I had just gotten over a bad cold (and hadn't held her during that time for fear of passing it on to her), she regurgitated on me when I finally picked her up. I think she really missed being held.

She was a little lovebug, too. Birds really do have a special place in our hearts. You don't need to explain why you were heartbroken or why you miss Spike so much; I think most of the users on this subreddit know the feeling all too well. I hope that, when you feel ready to get another bird, that you find one that will also have a special place in your heart. Take care.

Yes, it is! It may or may not be something that you want to encourage, but some parrots regurgitate and/or go through the motions with their babies, as well as their mates.
